{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABaRtJ3Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhD39IU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 61, "title": "Further reduce CI critical-path time with measured, coverage-preserving optimization", "body": "## Problem

Issue #59 / PR #60 successfully improved CI validation, but the current end-to-end GitHub Actions time is **still about 16 minutes** per revision. That is unnecessarily expensive for rapid, autonomous, repeated implement → review → fix → merge iterations. We need a **second, measured optimization that is actually implemented**, not just another performance report or a change that skips tests.

This Issue builds on, and must preserve, the improvements already merged by [PR #60](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/60). Do not revert the lossless bulk-array Playwright transport, the full 64-group coverage inventory, or independent native/browser jobs.

## Expected outcome

**Materially shorten full pre-merge CI wall-clock latency again, while keeping every mandatory test, assertion, fixture, negative control, security check and publish gate intact.**

- **Primary performance target:** aim for **under 10 minutes end-to-end** on comparable GitHub-hosted runners (roughly 40% faster than the most recent 16m07s run).
- **Stretch target:** **8 minutes or less** if the measured bottlenecks permit it without fragile complexity.
- Performance targets are engineering goals, **not permission to change the measured workload, ignore failures or introduce a flaky hard wall-time CI pass/fail threshold**. The delivered implementation must show a substantial, credible improvement; if the numerical targets prove infeasible, provide independently reproducible measurements, the best verified speedup, and a concrete evidence-backed explanation of the remaining critical path. Do not mark an instrumentation-only change or negligible speedup as completion.

All work, review and pre-merge verification must be executable autonomously; no mandatory human confirmation, real BIOS, copyrighted media, physical Sega hardware, subjective visual/audio sign-off, live Pages check or GitWeave/workflow-owner investigation.

## Context and reproduction

Repository: `takahirox/saturn-rust`. Latest checked `main`: `7b4a60a35ca4934c2246fa3128c31e2da60a78f5`.

### Actual hosted timing baseline

From [the post-PR-#60 main run](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/40484306388), completed successfully on 2026-10-27:

| Job / step | Duration |
| --- | ---: |
| **Full workflow, including publication** | **16m07s** |
| `build` (Wasm + Chromium) job | 15m39s |
| Chromium/browser validation step (including browser setup, runner regressions and full suite) | **13m11s / 791s** |
| Wasm/browser build step | 2m09s / 129s |
| `native` job | 8m47s / 527s |
| Native Rust check step (build, **988** tests, Clippy) | 8m26s / 506s |
| Artifact staging plus actual Pages deploy | ~19s combined |

The [preceding PR run](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/40482246109) passed with an overall duration ~15m02s, a 12m53s browser-validation step and a 9m47s native-check step. Hosted runner and test-duration variance matters.

The first optimization's independent [diagnosis](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/ci-performance.md) and [machine-readable timings](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/ci-performance-results.json) show that Playwright numeric-array serialization was a dominant **previous** problem and has been addressed. **Remaining guest execution** now consumes considerable time. The documented compact local medians include SCSP MVOL (~39.6s), display modes (~36.7s), HLE player (~24.7s), high-resolution rotation (~22.7s) and video transactions (~13.1s). These are local figures and must not be assumed to equal hosted bottlenecks.

Existing implementation/evidence:
- [`.github/workflows/pages.yml`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/.github/workflows/pages.yml): two independently running mandatory `native` and `build` jobs; Pages `site` depends on **both** and uses the **exact tested web artifact**; `deploy` publishes only the current `main`, never a PR.
- [`scripts/browser-smoke.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/browser-smoke.mjs), [`scripts/browser-groups.json`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/browser-groups.json), [`scripts/browser-timings.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/browser-timings.mjs) and [`scripts/browser-transport.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/browser-transport.mjs): complete 64-group Playwright suite, always-on performance instrumentation and lossless data transfer.
- [`scripts/ci-runner.test.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/ci-runner.test.mjs): existing failure-propagation, parity, coverage-manifest and Pages-gating regressions.
- [`scripts/check-fixtures.sh`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/check-fixtures.sh): the complete registered 90-fixture reproducibility checks.
- [`Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/Cargo.toml): native test profile currently uses `opt-level = 1` with debug assertions and overflow checks.
- [`docs/setup.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/setup.md): supported local/full-suite commands.

### Investigation and implementation directions

1. **Reprofile the current compact-transport head** rather than reusing the pre-#59 diagnosis: separate native compilation, individual Rust test binaries/guest workloads, browser launch/initialization, each of the 64 browser groups, actual in-browser Wasm guest clock execution, host/Playwright protocol work, polling, tool installation, job scheduling and artifact handoff. Identify the actual critical path.
2. Evaluate safe, **bounded parallel browser sharding** across independently initialized contexts/processes/jobs where demonstrably independent. Shared UI/media/backup/game state and sequential command traces must stay together or be isolated in their own fresh fixture. Compare sharding overhead, increased hosted runner usage, and aggregate versus critical-path runtime. Consider splitting the existing `browser-smoke.mjs` into deterministic subset entry points driven by a manifest while preserving **full-suite as the default** and enabling reproducible selected-group execution for profiling. Never shard by blindly concurrently invoking callbacks against one shared page.
3. Evaluate targeted improvements to the most expensive native and Wasm guest execution paths **without modifying architectural behavior**: repeated fixture initialization, avoidable harness allocations/copies, unnecessary browser crossings, excessive redundant cold boots only when identical assertions remain, or safe internal emulator hot-path optimizations proven bit/clock/IRQ/PCM/pixel equivalent. Do not reduce guest clock counts, test operands, expected results or emulated timing for speed. Avoid hardcoded guest-specific shortcuts.
4. Consider parallel Rust integration test binaries, test compilation/cache reuse and job decomposition only if measured end-to-end gains justify the complexity. Existing parallel `native`/`build` jobs are not themselves the fix; optimize the **slowest remaining required path**.
5. Implement the simplest maintainable high-impact change(s), measure again, and iterate until a material reduction is verified. Do not add a new test framework, paid hosted services, external backends or dependency-heavy machinery absent demonstrated value.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Baseline and hotspot evidence:** record at least one *actual* complete comparable GitHub Actions baseline, the current test-group manifest, per-Rust-binary and per-browser-group timings and the identified longest critical path. Include local comparison runs and state clearly what was/was not measured on GitHub.
- [ ] **Implemented, meaningful speedup:** land working code/CI changes that substantially reduce full end-to-end critical-path time. Target <10m on hosted CI, stretch <=8m. Use real before/after wall-clock measurements under comparable revision/tooling and repeat local or hosted runs where practical (ideally 3+). Report both per-stage and total timings, runner resource use and whether benefits persist under variance. Do not present extrapolated sums as executed runs.
- [ ] **No coverage loss:** all **64 original browser groups**, **988 existing Rust tests** (plus any added tests), **90 fixture builders**, the three original playable/diagnostic discs, native/Wasm/Canvas/AudioWorklet and every security, negative-control, reset/error, input, privacy, real pixel/PCM, media, IRQ/DMA and conformance assertion must still execute. New tests may increase counts. Audit and document exact original-to-new group coverage; no silent disappearance or replacing full-data assertions with hashes/sample checks.
- [ ] **Equivalent outputs and emulator clocks:** provide original-vs-optimized result parity at meaningful native guest/clock traces, browser Canvas pixels, PCM buffers, interrupt/DMA/exception states, and browser controls as relevant to the optimization. Do not change hardware timings, game behavior or accepted test data. Negative controls that previously detected incorrect emulation must continue to fail the deliberately incorrect paths.
- [ ] **Reliable isolation and error propagation:** sharded/parallel suites must be deterministic across scheduling and repeated runs. Missing groups/shards, corrupted assets, assertion failures, unhandled rejections, timeouts, crashed worker or cancelled required job must fail overall PR CI. No blanket retries, `|| true`, `catch`-and-ignore, ignored tests or hidden skips. The direct `npm run test:browser` command must still run *all* groups by default and correctly fail as a unit.
- [ ] **Bound resource usage and simplify debugging:** keep concurrency capped and documented for the target runner; report per-shard timing and failure group identity in logs; provide deterministic single-group/full-suite reproduction and a fallback to the existing lossless transport or original raw transport. Do not introduce flakiness, ordering dependence or impractical runner-memory use.
- [ ] **Preserve GitHub Pages safety:** PRs fully validate but never deploy. The current `main` alone may deploy *only* after **every** required native and browser suite/shard succeeds, using the precise tested site artifact. Maintain superseded-PR cancellation, serialized main publication, latest-main guard, `web/` allowlist, `/saturn-rust/` prefix, local-file privacy and no proprietary assets.
- [ ] **Final-tree mandatory checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target and Wasm Clippy (`-D warnings`), `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, `node --test scripts/ci-runner.test.mjs`, and a complete `npm run test:browser`; all must pass without skipped mandatory tests. Execute the PR GitHub Actions workflow and verify all required jobs pass before merging; no human log inspection required.
- [ ] **Regression safety and documentation:** extend runner/CI regression tests to intentionally fail a real shard/assertion and prove propagation to aggregate CI, including missing-shard and stale-artifact/publish-gate cases. Update `docs/ci-performance.md`, measurement data and `docs/setup.md` with executed before/after results, CPU/memory/job concurrency, remaining bottlenecks and reproduction commands.

## Optional validation

Additional isolated-runner or hardware profiles, alternative CPU-aware test orchestration, deeper emulator profiling, and low-risk caching experiments may improve confidence. Treat future performance ideas as separate follow-up tasks if the measured complexity outweighs the gain. Do not add real hardware, proprietary firmware, live Pages inspection or subjective human testing requirements.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Pre-merge local/PR CI must provide complete automated validation and performance evidence. Ordinary main GitHub Pages deployment remains gated by the existing workflow, but a post-merge live-site check or human approval is not required.
